title: vertebra-xray-core: identifiable three-dimensional Cobb angles from biplanar spine radiographs
description:
A measurement core for spinal deformity, accompanying Institute of One research note IORN-014.

Four endplate corners per view constrain only two of the three rotations that define a vertebra's orientation, so a three-dimensional Cobb angle computed from biplanar endplate landmarks alone is not identifiable. Adding the two pedicle centroids, already visible on the frontal view and the basis of the Nash-Moe and Perdriolle gradings, closes the system exactly.

The package implements the measurement layer given landmarks: biplanar reconstruction of vertebral orientation, three definitions of the three-dimensional Cobb angle, structural curve detection, per-case uncertainty by bootstrap, vertebral orientation measured from CT segmentation masks, a normative pedicle table from 394 VerSe vertebrae, and phantoms with closed-form angles. Landmark detection from pixels is out of scope by design.

No patient data are contained or redistributed. Validation uses synthetic phantoms and the public VerSe collection, which is read where it lives; no image from it is reproduced.
